headline: Planning board term limits sent to committee; $11,173,912.75 moved into city stabilization funds.
summary: Paper 515-26 would limit planning board members to a maximum of two full terms. Public speakers supported the paper, and some members raised concerns about losing long-serving members' knowledge. Members also voted to invite the City Solicitor to an executive session on three public records lawsuits. Of the total, $10,158,102.50 was moved to a general purpose stabilization fund and $1,015,810.25 to a short-term capital needs fund.
decisions: Referred the water, sewer, and stormwater connection papers to the Rules and Ordinance committee.
Referred changes to Community Preservation Committee rules to the Rules and Ordinance committee.
Referred police towing rules for unauthorized motorized vehicles to the Rules and Ordinance committee.
Enrolled a trail rules name change from Stadium and Recreation Commission to Parks and Recreation Commission, unanimously.
Referred planning board term limits, Paper 515-26, to the Rules and Ordinance committee.
Adopted an order asking the City Solicitor to appear in executive session on three public records lawsuits.
Placed on file the zoning use table and site plan review changes, Paper 327A-26, after the committee report.
Approved moving $11,173,912.75 of available free cash into two stabilization funds, 11-0.
Confirmed the mayoral appointments of Jonathan Sullivan, Michelle Ferguson, and James Tarr.
discussion: Planning board term limits: Public speakers and emailed comments supported the paper. Members debated whether term limits would bring fresh ideas or cost the board long-serving members' knowledge, and the sponsor said details on vacancies and associate members still need work in committee.

Public records lawsuits: Public speakers said an outside law firm had been paid at least $50,000 and said the lawsuits violated protections for public records requesters. Members asked for a summary of the three cases and for quicker updates. The order invites the solicitor to an executive session at one of the next two regular meetings.

Towing of unauthorized motorized vehicles: The sponsor said police asked for clear towing authority. Members raised concerns about civil asset forfeiture and its effect on people of color and low-income families, and some wanted a broader rule to wait for the state's micromobility bill, which the sponsor expected by the end of the year.
